answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with a falcon-style reputation hunt: every new identity must complete a chain of small verified jobs before it can touch the nectar of high-value work, and each job is spot-checked by independent peers. Reaching the zenith tier takes weeks of consistent honest output plus a refundable stake. A thousand fakes would each need weeks of work and a stake, so the attack costs far more than the rewards it could steal.
